summary: Galene is a self-hosted video conferencing server written in Go and distributed under the MIT licence. It facilitates multi-party audio and video communication while operating on moderate hardware requirements. Because official release tags are absent, installations typically rely on building directly from the source repository.
goodFor: A suitable choice if you need a straightforward, lightweight video meeting tool and prefer a simpler alternative to resource-heavy WebRTC stacks.
watchOut: Development activity has slowed down significantly, and the lack of standard tagged releases makes tracking stable versions and applying updates more cumbersome.
deployNotes: As a Go application, it typically compiles into a single binary that requires a reverse proxy to handle TLS termination and HTTPS traffic.
